title: Officer pool for delegation reads the users row, so officers seated through elections or appointments are never eligible
evidence: eligibleOfficerQuery: User::where('users.organization_id', ...)->where('users.role', 'SBO_OFFICER')->where('users.account_status', 'active')...->whereColumn('sbo_positions.title', 'users.position_title'); officerPayload: 'role' => $officer->role, 'position_title' => $officer->position_title (profile not activated, so these are the users-row values); TaskDelegationService::recommend line 75: User::where('users.organization_id', $organizationId)->where('users.role', 'SBO_OFFICER'). ElectionHandoverService::grant and OfficerAppointmentService activation write only AccountProfile (role, position_title), and User::booted notes 'an election hand over moves the profile and leaves these columns behind'.
impact: A student who wins an SBO seat (or anyone holding an SBO_OFFICER profile in an organization other than their users-row home) shows up in the Tasks page officer list (UserController lists by membership profile), but recommendOfficer sends Python role=STUDENT / null position so they are ranked invalid_role or missing_position, eligibleOfficerQuery excludes them so store/update return 'not an active SBO Officer', and the event planner (TaskDelegationService) omits them entirely. After every election handover the Admin cannot delegate tasks to the new officers, and officers who stepped down can still be scored from stale users-row columns.
suggested_fix: Build every delegation pool from AccountProfile rows for the organization (role = SBO_OFFICER, account_status = active, position_title in active sbo_positions), as OrganizationRecipients does, and read role, account_status and position_title from that profile in officerPayload, ineligibleEvaluation, eligibleOfficerQuery and TaskDelegationService::recommend. Add a feature test that seats an officer through ElectionHandoverService and assigns them a task.
verifier_notes: eligibleOfficerQuery (TaskController:732) and TaskDelegationService::recommend (:75) filter on users.role/users.organization_id/users.position_title. ElectionHandoverService::grant (line 207-215) writes only AccountProfile, and User::getRoleAttribute/getPositionTitleAttribute fall back to the users row when no profile is activated on the loaded instance, so a seated student keeps users.role=STUDENT and is excluded from store/update and the planner; officerPayload sends the stale row values to Python. No test covers handover followed by assignment.

title: Workflow confirm re-ranks each task after creating the earlier ones, so reviewed plans fail or log accepted picks as overrides
evidence: foreach ($data['tasks'] as $sequence => $draft) { $recommendation = $this->delegation->recommend($event->organization_id, $draft['title'], 'workflow', ...); ... if ($assignedTo === null || ! collect($recommendation['rankings'])->contains('officer_id', (int) $assignedTo)) { abort(422, "No officer is currently available for '{$draft['title']}'. ..."); } ... Task::create([... 'assigned_to' => $assignedTo ...]); ... 'action' => (int) $assignedTo === (int) $recommendedId ? 'accepted_recommendation' : 'overrode_recommendation'
impact: Each Task::create inside the transaction raises the officer's active count and sets assigned_at = now (recency 0), and the next recommend() call sees it. generatePlan ranks every draft task independently, so one officer is often rank 1 for many tasks. If the Admin picks that officer for more tasks than the open-task limit allows, the whole save is rolled back with 'No officer is currently available', even though the preview listed that officer as eligible. With fewer tasks, the stored scores differ from the preview and later picks are audited as 'overrode_recommendation' although the Admin chose the officer the screen recommended.
suggested_fix: Compute every task's ranking once, before the loop, from the same pre-save state the preview used, and store those numbers. Separately, validate the summed new assignments per officer against max_active_tasks and return a 422 that names the officer and the count. In generatePlan, show the planned load per officer and, when ranking, count the draft's earlier assignments toward workload so the preview matches what confirm enforces.
verifier_notes: confirmWorkflow (EventController:937) calls recommend() per draft inside the transaction after Task::create of earlier drafts; Task::saving sets assigned_at=now, so active count and recency (0) shift for later drafts. An officer chosen past max_active_tasks fails the rankings contains() check and aborts the whole save with the generic 'No officer is currently available' 422, and recommended_officer_id can change so a preview-recommended pick is audited as overrode_recommendation. Enforcing the cap itself is correct; the defects are the misleading error, preview/confirm drift and the audit label.

title: Date-only task deadlines turn tasks overdue at 00:05 on their due day and lower the assignee's performance score
evidence: <Input type="date" value={form.deadline} .../> sent as deadline: form.deadline (e.g. '2026-11-20', stored as 2026-11-20 00:00 by the datetime cast); MarkOverdueTasks: Task::whereIn('status', ['pending', 'in_progress'])->where('deadline', '<', now())->update(['status' => 'overdue']) scheduled dailyAt('00:05'); TaskDelegationService: $performanceScore = round($completed / ($completed + $overdue) * 100, 2)
impact: A task due 'Nov 20' becomes overdue five minutes into Nov 20, so the officer loses the whole due day. While it is overdue it counts as a failure in the performance factor of every later delegation ranking. A task created with today's date (allowed by after_or_equal:today) is overdue at the next run.
suggested_fix: Either send an end-of-day timestamp for date-only input (deadline = `${date}T23:59:59` in the organization's timezone) or switch the create and edit forms to the datetime-local input already used by the workflow editor. Also make the server normalise a bare date to endOfDay() before saving.
verifier_notes: TasksPage create (559) and edit (1015) use type=date; Task casts deadline as datetime so '2026-11-20' is stored at 00:00; MarkOverdueTasks runs dailyAt 00:05 with deadline < now(); performance factor counts overdue. Nothing normalises to end of day.

title: Overdue tasks cannot be edited or reassigned because every edit resends a past deadline
evidence: 'deadline' => [...$required, 'date', 'after_or_equal:today'] (applied on update via rules(true) as sometimes|required); TasksPage handleEditSubmit always sends deadline: editForm.deadline, prefilled from the stored deadline
impact: To fix the title or reassign an overdue task to another officer (the main reason to edit one), the Admin also has to move the deadline into the future, or the save fails with a deadline validation error. The Admin cannot reassign an overdue task while keeping its real due date.
suggested_fix: On update, apply after_or_equal:today only when the deadline actually changes (compare with $task->deadline), or let the client send deadline only when the field was edited.
verifier_notes: rules(true) keeps 'after_or_equal:today' as sometimes|required; handleEditSubmit always sends deadline prefilled from the stored value, so any task whose due date is before today fails validation on every edit including a pure reassignment.

title: Editing an event workflow task drops its time of day and skips the phase rule
evidence: deadline: isoToLocalDateTimeInput(task.deadline).slice(0, 10), then updateTask(..., { deadline: editForm.deadline }); TaskController::update never calls deadlineMatchesPhase for tasks with a phase
impact: Saving any edit (even just the title) on a workflow task due 'event day 14:00' rewrites the deadline to 00:00 that day, before the event starts, which breaks the event_day rule that confirmWorkflow enforces. Post-event tasks can likewise move outside the 30-day window. The deadlines the confirm step validated are silently corrupted.
suggested_fix: Edit deadlines with a datetime-local input that keeps the stored time. In TaskController::update, when the task has a phase and event_id, check the new deadline against the same phase window confirmWorkflow uses.
verifier_notes: openEditTask slices isoToLocalDateTimeInput(task.deadline) to 10 chars and handleEditSubmit always resends it, so a workflow task's time is reset to 00:00; TaskController::update never checks phase (deadlineMatchesPhase is only in EventController). An event_day task at 14:00 becomes 00:00, before start_time.

title: Reassigning on edit skips the open-task limit and records the chosen officer as the recommendation
evidence: if (! empty($data['assigned_to'])) { $assignee = $this->eligibleOfficerQuery($request)->where('school_id', $data['assigned_to'])->first(); ... $data = $this->applyAssignmentScoring($data, $assignee, $request); } ; assignmentScores fallback: 'recommended_officer_id' => $assignee->school_id, 'rankings' => [$local]
impact: store() only accepts an officer from the eligible rankings, but update() accepts any active officer with a position, including one already at max_active_tasks. The edit drawer lists every officer. The stored delegation_snapshot then says this officer was the recommended one, with a workload score of 0, so the audit trail claims a recommendation that never happened, and no task_recommendations rows or audit log are written for the reassignment.
suggested_fix: In update(), run recommendOfficer() with the task's title and category and reject an assigned_to that is not in lastDelegation['rankings'], as store() does. Persist task_recommendations and a task_delegated audit row for the reassignment, and keep the real recommended_officer_id.
verifier_notes: update() only uses eligibleOfficerQuery (no workload filter). assignmentScores either calls Python with a single-officer pool or falls back with recommended_officer_id = assignee, so delegation_snapshot names the chosen officer as recommended. No persistRecommendations, AiOutput or task_delegated AuditLog is written on update. Edit drawer lists every active SBO officer.

title: PUT /tasks/{id} changes status without the transition, dependency or progress-history rules
evidence: rules(true) includes 'status' => ['sometimes','required','in:pending,in_progress,completed,overdue'] and 'completed_at'; update() then calls $task->update($this->normalizeCompletionFields($data, $task)) with no canTransition() call, no depends_on_task_id check, and no recordProgressUpdate()
impact: updateStatus blocks a dependency-blocked task from starting or completing and records history, but the same change sent through PUT marks a blocked workflow task completed (or completed to overdue), with no progress entry. This breaks the 'blocked tasks cannot start or complete' guarantee in docs/manage-tasks-workflow-use-case.md and changes the officer's performance score.
suggested_fix: Remove status, progress_percent and completed_at from the update rules, so status changes only go through updateStatus. Or route a status change in update() through canTransition, the dependency check and recordProgressUpdate.
verifier_notes: rules(true) accepts status/progress_percent/completed_at; update() skips canTransition, the depends_on_task_id check and recordProgressUpdate. The client edit form does not send status, so this is reachable through the API by the creator or an Admin only.

title: The Admin's 'Assigned category' is overridden by any title keyword from an earlier area
evidence: $haystack = strtolower($title.' '.($type ?? '')); foreach (self::POSITION_RELEVANCE_MAP as $area => $spec) { foreach ($spec['keywords'] as $keyword) { if (preg_match(...)) return $area; } } with TaskController passing $request->input('category') ?: $request->input('task_type') as $type (task_delegation.py infer_task_area behaves the same)
impact: The category is only appended to the title and the areas are checked in map order (finance, publicity, documentation, logistics, coordination). 'Print the attendance report' with category Logistics is scored as documentation, and 'Budget poster' with Publicity is scored as finance. The category select on the create form has no effect whenever the title contains a keyword from an earlier area, so the ranking and the stored explanation describe the wrong task area.
suggested_fix: When a valid category (one of the five map keys) is supplied, use it as the area directly and infer from the title only when the category is absent. Change infer_task_area in Python and inferArea in PHP together and extend AiFallbackParityTest with a category-versus-title case.
verifier_notes: inferArea / infer_task_area append the category to the title and return the first area in map order whose keyword matches; 'Print the attendance report' + logistics matches 'report' (documentation) before 'logistic', 'Budget poster' + publicity matches 'budget' (finance). The category select is therefore ignored whenever an earlier area's keyword is in the title.

title: Event plans can be generated and confirmed for cancelled events, notifying officers of tasks for an event that will not happen
evidence: generatePlan checks only $event->start_time->lte(now()->addMinutes(5)) and an accepted workflow; confirmWorkflow checks only ownership and decision_status === 'pending'; neither reads $event->status (planning, approved, ongoing, completed, cancelled)
impact: The planner dropdown lists every event. An Admin can draft and save a to-do list for a cancelled event, which creates pending tasks, counts them toward officers' workload in later rankings, and sends 'New Event Workflow Task' notifications. A pending draft for an event cancelled after drafting can also still be confirmed.
suggested_fix: Return 409 from generatePlan and confirmWorkflow when the event status is cancelled or completed, and filter those events out of the planner dropdown in EventsPage.
verifier_notes: generatePlan checks only start_time and an accepted workflow; confirmWorkflow checks only ownership/pending. Neither reads event status, and the planner select lists every loaded event (EventsPage 1510). A future-dated cancelled event can get a plan, tasks and notifications.

title: Schedule-conflict detection counts cancelled events
evidence: $conflicts = Event::where('organization_id', $event->organization_id)->whereKeyNot($event->id)->where('start_time', '<', $event->end_time)->where('end_time', '>', $event->start_time)->get([...]) (no status filter)
impact: Cancelled events go to the model as schedule_conflicts, and the template fallback lists them as 'Overlaps with ...', so the plan's 'Possible problems' section warns about clashes with events that will not take place.
suggested_fix: Add ->where('status', '!=', 'cancelled') (and exclude rejected approval states if they apply) to the conflict query.
verifier_notes: Conflict query (EventController:759) has no status filter, and templateWorkflow turns each into 'Overlaps with ...'.

title: Removing a workflow to-do leaves a hidden dependency that blocks saving
evidence: function removeWorkflowTask(index) { setWorkflowDraft((current) => ({ ...current, tasks: current.tasks.filter((_, taskIndex) => taskIndex !== index) })); } while later tasks keep depends_on_key; server: if (! empty($task['depends_on_key']) && (! $keyPositions->has($task['depends_on_key']) ...)) return 422 "'{$task['title']}' can only start after a task listed above it."
impact: Template and AI plans chain most tasks to 'confirm-plan'. Deleting that item leaves the other tasks pointing at a key that no longer has an option, so the select shows no dependency but the save fails with a message about ordering that the Admin cannot see or fix from the form.
suggested_fix: In removeWorkflowTask, clear depends_on_key on every remaining task whose dependency was the removed key, or point it at the removed task's own dependency.
verifier_notes: removeWorkflowTask only filters the array; dependants keep depends_on_key; the select then has no matching option and confirmWorkflow returns the ordering 422. templateWorkflow chains announce-event, prepare-venue and confirm-budget to 'confirm-plan'.

title: N+1 queries per officer per task in delegation scoring, run inside the confirm transaction
evidence: foreach ($officers as $officer) { $base = Task::where(...)->where('assigned_to', $officer->school_id); $active = (clone $base)->...->count(); $completed = ...->count(); $overdue = ...->count(); $daysSinceAssignment = $this->daysSinceLastAssignment(...) } called once per draft task in generatePlan (line 834) and again per task inside DB::transaction in confirmWorkflow (line 937); TaskController::officerPayload runs about six queries per candidate and is called again by the eligible filter, localAssignmentScores and ineligibleEvaluation
impact: A nine-task plan in an organization with 20 officers runs about 9 x 20 x 4 = 720 count queries to generate and the same again while holding the confirm transaction. A single recommendation preview runs 100+ queries. This slows the page the planner prompt already describes as waiting, and keeps confirm write locks open longer.
suggested_fix: Load per-officer counts once with a grouped query (SELECT assigned_to, SUM(status IN (...)), SUM(status='completed'), SUM(status='overdue'), MAX(assigned_at) ... GROUP BY assigned_to) and reuse it for every task in the plan. In TaskController, compute officerPayload once per officer and reuse it.
verifier_notes: recommend() runs 3-5 queries per officer per task (count x3 plus max(assigned_at)), called per draft in generatePlan and again per draft inside the confirm transaction; officerPayload runs ~5 queries and is re-run in the eligible filter and ineligibleEvaluation. Exact query counts in the impact are estimates.

title: 'Best officer role' is free text but the confirm step requires an exact, case-sensitive position title
evidence: <Input id={`workflow-role-${index}`} value={task.recommended_role || ''} ... placeholder="Example: Secretary" />; confirmWorkflow: ! $activePositions->containsStrict($task['recommended_role']) -> 422; the preview uses Rule::exists (case-insensitive on MySQL) and TaskDelegationService matches the role with strcasecmp
impact: If the Admin types 'secretary', 'Review officers' succeeds and steers to the Secretary, then Save fails with 'Choose an active officer role'. A typo fails the preview with a generic validation message. The Admin has to guess the exact spelling of an active position.
suggested_fix: Replace the input with a select of the organization's active SBO positions (already computed as allowed_positions in generatePlan; return it in the response), and compare case-insensitively on the server.
verifier_notes: Best officer role is a free-text Input (EventsPage 1583); confirmWorkflow uses containsStrict (case-sensitive), while the preview uses Rule::exists and recommend() uses strcasecmp. allowed_positions is already in structured_input context but not returned to the form.

title: Task create API accepts 'completed' or 'overdue' as the initial status, which changes the officer's performance score
evidence: 'status' => [...$required, 'in:pending,in_progress,completed,overdue'] used by store(); normalizeCompletionFields sets progress_percent 100 and completed_at now for completed
impact: The client offers only Pending and In progress, but the API creates a task already completed or overdue. That task immediately counts as completed or overdue history in the performance factor of every later ranking, so an officer's delegation standing can be raised or lowered without any work being done.
suggested_fix: On store(), restrict status to pending,in_progress (keep the wider set only for updateStatus).
verifier_notes: rules() used by store() allows completed and overdue; normalizeCompletionFields sets 100%/completed_at. Only reachable through the API (client offers pending/in_progress), by an Admin who passes the eligibility check.

title: One invalid workflow explanation discards the valid explanations for every other task
evidence: $isValid = $generated && $validIds === $returnedIds && $explanations->every(fn ... $this->ai->preservesNumericFacts($row['explanation'], $fact)); ... $explanation = $isValid ? trim($explanations[$task->id]['explanation']) : null;
impact: If the model gets one number wrong in a nine-task plan, all nine TASK_EXPLANATION records are marked failed and every task keeps only 'Rank N by deterministic weighted scoring.' The use case says each task gets its own explanation record and only invalid claims are rejected.
suggested_fix: Validate each returned explanation on its own and keep the ones that pass. Mark only the missing or invalid task explanations as failed, and count generated_count and failed_count accordingly.
verifier_notes: explainWorkflowAssignments computes a single $isValid over every explanation; one failing preservesNumericFacts row or a missing id nulls every explanation and marks all TASK_EXPLANATION rows failed; generated_count/failed_count are all-or-nothing.

title: Template fallback copy says the AI writer is unavailable when the model answered but its plan failed validation
evidence: if ($workflow === null && ! $isTemplate) { Log::warning(...); $isTemplate = true; $generated = ['data' => $this->templateWorkflow($event, $context), ...]; } with template overview 'Template draft: the AI writer is not available right now...'; the client ignores res.data.is_template, and requirements are cleared (setPlanForm({ ..., requirements: '' })) and never saved to planning_details
impact: When Groq returns a plan with an invalid deadline, the Admin is told the AI is down, the planning context they typed is silently ignored by the template and wiped from the form, and nothing in the history marks that draft as a template rather than an AI plan. Regenerating means retyping the context.
suggested_fix: Give the template a separate overview line for 'the suggested plan did not pass checks', show a template badge from is_template (and from context_version in history), and keep the requirements text in the form or save it to planning_details.requirements.
verifier_notes: Real: the template overview always says 'the AI writer is not available right now' even when the model answered but failed normalizeWorkflow; EventsPage never reads is_template; handleGeneratePlan clears requirements and generatePlan does not store them in planning_details, and templateWorkflow ignores them. Wrong: the record is marked as a template (context_version 'event-workflow-template-v1', model_name 'template-draft') and the typed requirements are kept in structured_input; the gap is only that the client shows neither.
corrected_fix: Give the validation-failed template its own overview line, show a template badge in the client from is_template (and from context_version/model_name on history entries), and keep the requirements text in the form after drafting (or store it in planning_details.requirements so selectPlanningEvent restores it). No new server-side template marker is needed.

title: After confirming one draft, the other drafts the server discarded still show as Pending and can be opened for editing
evidence: setWorkflowHistory((current) => current.map((output) => output.id === workflowOutputId ? { ...output, decision_status: 'accepted' } : output)); while confirmWorkflow on the server sets every other pending version to 'discarded'
impact: Clicking an older 'Draft N · Pending' button loads it as an editable plan. The Admin can spend time editing it, and saving then returns 409 'This draft has already been saved or removed.'
suggested_fix: After a successful confirm, mark every other pending entry as discarded locally or refetch getEventWorkflowHistory.
verifier_notes: After confirm the client updates only the confirmed entry; the server marks other pending versions discarded. History buttons load any locally 'pending' structured_output for editing, and saving it returns 409.

title: Confirm has no row lock, so two concurrent confirms of the same draft create duplicate task sets
evidence: if ($aiOutput->decision_status !== 'pending') { return 409 } is read before DB::transaction(...) and the draft row is never re-read with lockForUpdate inside it
impact: A confirm sent from two tabs, or retried after a slow response, passes the pending check twice. The event then gets two copies of every task, two notifications per officer and inflated workload counts.
suggested_fix: Inside the transaction, re-read the AiOutput with lockForUpdate(), abort 409 unless it is still pending, and also check that no accepted EVENT_WORKFLOW row exists for the event.
verifier_notes: The pending check runs before DB::transaction and the AiOutput row is never re-read with lockForUpdate; the accepted-workflow guard exists only in generatePlan. The client disables the button during the request, so this needs two tabs or a retry, hence low.

title: Event workflow tasks' delegation snapshot has a different shape, so the task screen hides its eligibility rules and engine
evidence: 'eligibility_rules' => ['required_role' => 'SBO_OFFICER', 'required_account_status' => 'active', 'requires_active_position' => true, 'max_active_tasks' => $maxActive] (associative) and no 'engine' key; TasksPage getDelegationDetail: Array.isArray(container.eligibility_rules) ? ... : null
impact: Standalone tasks show the eligibility rules list and the engine badge, but tasks saved from an event plan show neither. The same delegation is explained differently depending on how the task was created.
suggested_fix: Return the same list-of-strings eligibility_rules as TaskController::eligibilityRules (including 'officer must be marked available' and the max active tasks rule), and set 'engine' => 'php-service' in TaskDelegationService::recommend.
verifier_notes: TaskDelegationService::recommend returns associative eligibility_rules and no engine key; the snapshot is stored as delegation_snapshot and getDelegationDetail requires Array.isArray(eligibility_rules) and reads container.engine, so workflow tasks show neither.

title: Parity tests do not compare the score constants, and the only cross-engine score test skips when the engine is down
evidence: test_the_php_keyword_map_and_position_tiers_equal_the_python_engine_map compares only keywords/primary/secondary; PRIMARY 100 / RELATED 70 / UNRELATED 40 / UNKNOWN 55 / NEUTRAL_PERFORMANCE 70 / NEVER_ASSIGNED 100 and the eligibility order are checked only by test_php_task_fallback_matches_the_live_python_engine_on_the_same_officer, which calls markTestSkipped when the live service is unreachable
impact: In CI, where no live engine runs, a change to any tier score, the neutral prior, or the eligibility rules on one side passes, so the PHP fallback and Python can rank officers differently without any failing test.
suggested_fix: Extend the static parity test to parse and compare the numeric constants in task_delegation.py (PRIMARY_POSITION_MATCH_SCORE and the others) with TaskDelegationService's constants, and add a static fixture test that runs the same officer set through both engines' code paths.
verifier_notes: Real: the static parity test compares only keywords/primary/secondary, and the only cross-engine score comparison skips when the live service is down; CI's server job runs php artisan test with no AI service, so it always skips there. Overstated: pytest (ai-service CI job) pins some Python values (role 100/40, the weighted-sum formula, recency 0/50/100), and PHP tests pin the PHP side, so a change is not entirely untested; what is untested is drift between the two (e.g. UNKNOWN 55, NEUTRAL 70, eligibility order).
corrected_fix: Extend test_the_php_keyword_map_and_position_tiers_equal_the_python_engine_map to parse the Python numeric constants (PRIMARY_POSITION_MATCH_SCORE, RELATED_POSITION_MATCH_SCORE, UNRELATED_POSITION_SCORE, UNKNOWN_POSITION_SCORE, NEUTRAL_PERFORMANCE_SCORE) and compare them with TaskDelegationService's constants via reflection; optionally add a shared JSON fixture of officers plus expected rankings asserted by both pytest and PHPUnit so the comparison runs without a live service.
